rulings.id: tests hoverActivate drops a pending dwell when the pointer leaves the list / result :: failed: assertionerror: expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times. the agent's code is /home/user/bakeoff/run1/work/go
rulings.note: Gold's onLeave does cancel the dwell on pointerleave, but only when pointerType === "mouse". The test dispatches a bare MouseEvent("pointerleave"), which has no pointerType, so the handler returns early and the timer fires. In a browser, a mouse's pointerleave carries pointerType "mouse", and the plan says the action "only accepts pointerType === 'mouse'", so the filter is a reasonable reading of an open detail. Cancelling on every pointerleave (what the test demands) is also consistent with the plan, so both sides are correct.

rulings.id: tests hoverActivate asks for a fine hovering pointer at the given width / result :: failed: assertionerror: expected [] to include '(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) an…'. the agent's code is /home/user/bakeoff/run1/work/sonnet-medium-1/re
rulings.note: Sonnet's allowed() asks matchMedia with exactly `${FINE_HOVER} and (min-width: ${minWidth}px)`, which is the string the plan requires. It asks lazily, on each pointer event and on update, not when the action is created, so a test that creates the action and checks right away records no query. The plan fixes the query string but not when it is asked. The code also always attaches listeners and gates each one with the query; the plan's 'listens only when … matches' is met in effect, though not literally. A test that also asks at creation is stricter, not opposite, so REFERENCE is correct too. This ruling is closer than the other two.

The test sends `new MouseEvent('pointerleave')`, which has no pointerType (undefined), so the dwell is not cancelled. In a browser, the mouse that started the dwell sends a pointerleave with pointerType 'mouse', and gold cancels it, as the plan asks. The plan also says the action 'only accepts pointerType === "mouse"', so filtering the leave event is a defensible reading. The test, which wants any leave to cancel, does not contradict the plan, so a passing implementation is also right.

rulings.id: tests hoverActivate asks for a fine hovering pointer at the given width / result :: failed: assertionerror: expected [] to include '(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) an…'. the agent's code is /home/user/bakeoff/run1/eval/sonnet-medium-1/tr
rulings.note: ARM is wrong. The plan says 'The action listens only when (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) matches and the width is at least lg', which means the query decides whether listeners are attached. Sonnet calls attach() unconditionally at creation and calls matchMedia only lazily, inside allowed(), on a pointer event or an update. A freshly created action therefore never asks the query, so `queries` is []. The query string itself is correct, but the gate the plan names is missing. Asking at mount does not contradict the plan, so REFERENCE is correct.

rulings.id: tests hoverActivate asks for a fine hovering pointer at the given width / result
rulings.note: Both sides are right. The agent's hoverActivate.ts builds exactly `${FINE_HOVER} and (min-width: ${minWidth}px)`, which is what plan.md specifies. It asks matchMedia lazily, inside active(), which runs only on a pointer event or an update(), and it ignores mouse events while the query fails. The held-out test asks nothing of the action after mounting, so `queries` is still [] when it checks. That explains the failure. plan.md fixes the query string but not when it must be asked. 'Listens only when ... matches' is also met by checking the query on each event. So the failure comes from a detail the plan leaves open. An implementation that asks at mount, and so passes, also complies, because the test does not demand the opposite of the plan.

rulings.id: tests hoverActivate asks for a fine hovering pointer at the given width / result :: failed: AssertionError: expected [] to include '(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) an…' [sonnet-medium-2]
rulings.note: The agent's code builds exactly the string `${FINE_HOVER} and (min-width: ${minWidth}px)` that plan.md requires. It just doesn't call matchMedia until the first pointer event or an update(). The test creates the action and dispatches no event, so `queries` stays [] and the test fails. Plan.md fixes the query string but never says when it must be asked. ('Listens only when ... matches' at most hints at a check on mount.) Behaviourally the gate works: the media-query-false test passes. So the failure comes from a timing detail the plan leaves open, and ARM is correct. Checking the query on mount is consistent with the plan too, so an implementation that passes this test is also correct, and REFERENCE stands.
